extracted.intended_audience: extramural researchers, research administrators, and NIH applicants (Northwestern University community)
extracted.subtask_description: A library-maintained listing of targeted NIH news releases and policy updates relevant to extramural researchers and research administrators, with inclusion/exclusion rules and links to source notices. Meant to help applicants and institutional officials keep current on NIH application, reporting, and policy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: This section highlights targeted news releases from the NIH, including announcements from the NIH Extramural Nexus (News) site, which features announcements of funding, some changes in policy, updates to existing award structures, etc., and announcements from the main NIH news site (NIH News Releases) that are of interest to extramural researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide collects NIH announcements likely to affect extramural applicants and administrators and links to the original NIH pages (NIH News Releases and NIH Extramural Nexus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: What we will not include in this section: Announcements of research from NIH researchers (unless they have a call for proposals from extramural researchers for partnerships). This includes the NIH news publications NIH Research Matters, NIH News in Health, NIH Catalyst. These sources all feature intramural (NIH-based) work and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude intramural research announcements unless they explicitly contain calls/partnership opportunities for extramural researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMSP pilot format notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH has released a new 'pilot' Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMSP) format. The purpose of the new format is to simplify the DMSP for both applicants and study section reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the NIH's Data Management and Sharing Plan Format page for details. GalterLibrary resources (GalterGuide and class) have been updated to help complete the new format DMSP.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPOS Common Form and ORCID linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reminder about the Current and Pending (Other) Support (CPOS) Common Form: applicants should ensure their ORCID ID is linked to both their eRA Commons ID and NCBI / NCBI account to ensure successful completion of the forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Extramural Nexus 'You Ask, We Answer' article explains CPOS purpose and required application types; check linked CPOS FAQs and SciENcv Common Forms FAQs frequently for updates and helpful resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual MFTRP certification requirement (RPPR Section G.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals serving as senior/key personnel must certify annually to their participation or non-participation in a Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program (MFTRP) by uploading a certification statement in RPPR Section G.1, Special Notice of Award and Funding Opportunity Announcement Reporting Requirements. This requirement is IN ADDITION to the certifications individuals make within the NIH Common Forms for biosketch and Other Support (OS) documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated FAQ: individuals who have submitted a Common Form biosketch or Other Support document in which they have certified for MFTRP do NOT have to complete the annual MFTRP as a separate document for progress reports in section G.1. If an investigator is not submitting Common Form documents (under the period of leniency through May 2026), they will be required to submit a separate MFTRP certification document and should follow the instructions in the linked notice. The certification statement language included in the RPPR must align with the statement within the Common Forms and state: 'I [insert name] certify that, at the time of submission, I am not a party to a malign foreign talent recruitment program.' The file for each senior/key person must be named 'MFTRPcert_[Name].pdf' where '[Name]' is the name of the senior/key person, and the PDF must be flattened prior to upload. (NOT-OD-26-018). See the RPPR Instruction Guide (page 116) for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted timeline / period of leniency for Common Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of help desk requests and technical problems placing a burden on the community, the NIH is allowing a 'period of leniency' through May 2026. During this time, applicants may submit either the Common Forms or the older forms for biosketch and other support documents; a warning will still be issued when submitting the older forms, but applications will not be blocked or withdrawn from submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This leniency also applies to Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs), Just-in-Time (JIT) and Prior Approval (PA) submissions and allows certifications on the Common Forms to align with the Research Security Training outlined in NOT-OD-26-017.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Apply — Application Guide updates (required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH updated its How to Apply - Application Guide to incorporate significant changes to the application process, including the NIH Biosketch Common Form and NIH Biosketch Supplement, the Current and Pending (Other) Support (CPOS) Common Form, the ORCID requirement, and foreign justification attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the updated Application Guide and the news announcement for details and links to resources and materials to guide the application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on omitted attachments and applicant contact
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH will contact applicants in limited situations when files or attachments have been omitted (e.g., leaving out required sections of applications, incorrect files being uploaded). The NIH will NOT accept requests for changes to already submitted sections (research section, budget, etc.); nor will it accept unsolicited attachments or applicant requests to replace materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIH will contact the applicant's Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) who must provide the missing materials within a timeframe. Applicants should not contact the NIH directly. Details are provided in NOT-OD-26-025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship application guidance — consult current Forms-I
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated NIH Fellowship Resources: fellowships are open to early career scientists and applicants are reminded to consult instructions for current application forms (Forms-I) when preparing fellowship proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the updated 'Focus on Fellowships' video series and the current application form instructions for accurate application preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency modifications to NIH peer review — decision grouping and simplified statements
rubrics_metrics.description: To address a backlog, NIH announced modifications to speed up peer review. Review panels will consider proposals in three groups: (1) Competitive and discussed (at the meeting) and considered for funding; (2) Competitive and not discussed, but considered for funding; (3) Not competitive and not discussed - not considered for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review summary statements will be simplified. The announcement encourages researchers to accept requests to serve on review sections ('say yes'). These are operational changes to how reviews are triaged and how summary statements will appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified NIH funding strategy tenets for award decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will implement steps toward a unified strategy to guide clearer and consistent funding decisions across Institutes, Centers, and Offices (ICOs). ICOs should adhere to tenets such as considering budget, NIH's priorities, and merit (among others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing an Executive Order, NIH will still consider peer review but move away from paylines. See NIH Grants & Funding — Funding Decisions page for details on how decisions will be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: New application and award structure for NIH-funded international collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective for due dates on or after January 25, 2026, competing applications that request funding for one or more foreign components must be in response to a funding opportunity using a new grant type (replacing foreign subawards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NOT-OD-25-155 for full instructions and implications for applications requesting international components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing official verification of grant assignment accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing officials should verify the accuracy of their grant assignments to departments or components within institutions of higher education in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any corrections must be made by the stated deadline (example given: by 8:00 PM EDT on Monday, October 6, 2025) to be reflected in NIH annual reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Confidentiality (CoC) System requests accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH, with OMB approval under the Paperwork Reduction Act, is accepting requests in the CoC System for Research Not Funded by NIH and Institutional Official verifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational notice for institutions needing CoC system access and verifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-Cost Extension functionality in eRA Commons re-enabled
rubrics_metrics.description: No-Cost Extension functionality has been re-enabled in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational update for grant administration workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Scientific Data Sharing information centralized on Grants & Funding site
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s scientific data sharing policies and data repositories information can now be found on the NIH Grants & Funding site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose of the move is to centralize resources so grant applicants can more easily find data sharing requirements and repository guidance when preparing awards.
